name: Make a tarp shelter
blurb: A tarp and four metres of cord give you a dozen configurations for rain, wind and sun. Fast, light and far more adaptable than a tent.
gear: Guy lines and a ridgeline cord
steps: Learn the A-frame: a taut ridgeline between two trees, tarp over it, corners pegged out. The default all-weather setup.
Learn the lean-to: one edge high, one at the ground, open side away from the wind — best for a fire in front.
Learn the diamond or plough point for a fast single-person shelter with one anchor.
Master the ridgeline: a taut-line hitch at one end for adjustment, a trucker’s hitch for tension.
Pitch it low and tight in wind, high and open in heat.
Practise pitching in the dark and in rain — that is when you will actually need it.
tips: A sagging ridgeline collects a puddle that eventually collapses the shelter. Get it drum tight.
Watch what the wind is doing before choosing your orientation, not after.
proof: You pitch three different configurations in under five minutes each, and stay dry through real rain.
